  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Replicating the GSS application}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Nepaul and Stern (2026) estimate The Nepaul-Stern Model of Attitude Stability and Constraint on six GSS Likert items, using four stacked rotating panels from 2006 to 2020: ideological identification, military spending, welfare spending, the number of immigrants, party identification, and environmental spending. The replication program reads `gss2.prn`, collapses person-waves to people, and uses a common time grid

```{r}
gss_time_grid <- c(2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10)
```

rather than each respondent's own interview date. The gaps are the differences of this grid: 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2. Those integers are the exponents on the persistence matrix.

The file contains 11,282 people. The likelihood keeps 11,252 of them. The Likert answers are coded `1, ..., K` with `K` equal to 7, 3, 3, 5, 7, 3. Party identification is stored as 0 through 6 in the text file and enters the likelihood as 1 through 7. The intercept of each attitude is fixed at zero because the model includes a wave effect for every attitude, and the loading of the environment item on the second factor is fixed at zero.

A full re-estimation is a few hundred likelihood evaluations of about eleven thousand people. The script `validation/run_gss.R` does that job. It is not run when the package is checked. The call it makes has this shape.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fit <- attitudedyn(
  cbind(ideology, military, welfare, immigrants, party, environment) ~
    0 + `(Intercept)` + age + hs + college + adv + female + white + black +
    inc_mid + inc_high,
  data = gss,
  id = ~ id,
  wave = ~ wave,
  time_grid = c(2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10),
  weights = weight,
  n_factors = 2,
  draws = 10,
  start = estimates,
  control = attitudedyn_control(n_threads = 20, maxit = 0, vcov = "none",
                                use_gradient = FALSE, keep_scores = FALSE)
)
```

The constant is 1 on a wave that is in the text file and 0 on a wave that is only there because it sits between a person's first and last waves. `validation/run_gss.R` builds that column and evaluates the shipped coefficients.

The replication program reports a log-likelihood of -111,389.88 at the shipped coefficients and at that run's random draws. A different random-number generator will not reproduce those digits. `validation/compare_gss` checks the likelihood on the same prepared sample and the same draws. On that comparison the likelihoods agree.
